thread:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - region-us-east error_rate spike detected. rule=region_request_error_rate, value=6.8% (3m avg) — paging oncall. link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd123/region-health

alex (oncall): seeing the page. looking at grafana, errors started ~03:07 UTC. can anyone triage root cause? @jordan can you pull ingress logs and svc health?

jordan (sre): diving in. prelim logs show a burst of 503s from the transform-service cluster in us-east-1, coming from a subset of nodes. suspecting a rolling host-level network flap or a bad kernel update on a small pool. tailing logs now: ``instance=transf-12 host=ip-10-2-7-45 status=503 "upstream reset"``

maya (infra): I see many artifacts in the node exporter metrics around the same time — NIC drops and then some kubelet restarts on node group tg-transforms-eu1. Could be a bad host image rollout that hit 3 instances.

alex (oncall): for mitigation: 1) remove tg-transforms-eu1 from LB pool, 2) scale up transforms in us-east to absorb, 3) fail traffic to us-west if latency acceptable. I'll start 1 & 2, @maya can you handle LB removal & node group rollback?

maya (infra): removing tg-transforms-eu1 from LB now. also reverting instance template to previous AMI and triggering re-create.

jordan (sre): scaling transforms up by +4 pods, changing HPA target. also pushing temporary service-level circuit breaker to reduce retries (to avoid thundering herd). snippet: ```kubectl patch hpa transforms --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'```

monitoring-bot: :white_check_mark: LB pool update successful. 3 nodes drained.

alex (oncall): update: error rate down to 3.2% and trending. customers affected: quick scan shows ~18 customers saw elevated 5xx in that window (mostly low-RPS accounts). @sam can you prep a short customer-impact note if we need to notify?

sam (cs): drafting note now. will ping the accounts with >1% error impact in last 15m. cc'ing account owners.

lina (product): any user-visible feature regressions we should be aware of?

jordan (sre): not feature regressions, transient 503s only. no data loss. KV cache warmups were impacted but recovered after nodes drained.

alex (oncall): planning immediate post-incident changes to reduce noisy alerts and prevent recurrence:
- adjust region_request_error_rate alert to require min_samples > 10 and evaluation window 5m (was 3m).
- add a derivative check for host-level NIC drop spikes to correlate host flaps.
- create a multi-region traffic-shift dashboard panel showing percent traffic per region with alert if shift > 15% in 10m.

jordan (sre): proposing new alert rule (prometheus style):
```
ALERT RegionErrorRateHigh
IF sum by(region)(increase(requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]))
/ sum by(region)(increase(requests_total[5m])) > 0.075
FOR 5m
ANNOTATIONS { runbook = "runbooks/region-error-rate.md" }
```
This uses a 5m window and 7.5% threshold. also add `min_over_time(requests_total[5m]) > 10` guard to avoid noise for small customers.

maya (infra): agree. also we should mute node-level alerts during autoscaling/rolling updates to avoid pager storms; add an alert-suppression label during autoscale events.

alex (oncall): I'll make a realtime change: mute the lower-severity host NIC alert for 30m and raise the threshold on region_request_error_rate to 7.5% now to avoid follow-up noise while we stabilize.

monitoring-bot: :mute: Alert "host_nic_drop" muted for 30m by alex.

jordan (sre): created ticket RD-4821 to track follow-ups: alert tuning, grafana panels, canary checks per region. adding tasks:
- Add multi-region failover monitor (synthetic canary) that runs every 1m and validates end-to-end on model endpoints (owner: eng-runtime)
- Dashboard: region ratio + per-region 95th latency + 5xx heatmap (owner: observability)
- Runbook update: explicit LB drain & rollback steps (owner: infra)

sam (cs): sent initial notes to the affected accounts and created a status update for the status page (no ongoing impact).

lina (product): thanks — can we get a short post-incident summary for ELT team and partners? say impact window, root cause, mitigations and next steps.

alex (oncall): will draft PI summary and tag owners. handing off oncall to maya for next 4h as I'm out for rest of shift. please continue watch and escalate if error_rate > 8% or any new region shows >10% traffic shift.

maya (infra): taking over. monitoring endpoints and the LB. I'll follow up in 30m with status or sooner if anything changes.

jordan (sre): note for after-hours: add a small hysteresis in the failover policy to require sustained cross-region latency >200ms for 3m before auto-failover. too-aggressive failover caused additional load this morning in another incident.

alex (oncall): agreed. action items assigned in RD-4821. closing thread for now, will postmortem draft in #postmortems tomorrow. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
